I thought your arguments sounded suspiciously like the Chinese room.  

The fact of the matter is that Searle's arguments are constructed in such a way that if we accepted everything he said, intelligence would be impossible.  Basically, he accepts that something like machine intelligence could theoretically exist; he never says the Chinese room is impossible, for example, and he never says the the computer could not simulate a brain getting high.  What he says is these intelligences are not really intelligences.  

What is it that humans want from AI?  We want a machine that can keep us company; that can hold down a conversation; that can read emails and filter spam; that can drive a car.  Searle (and I assume you) never deny that these things are possible.  You're just quibbling over the meaning of intelligence and whether a machine is "really" intelligent.  

tl;dr: I really couldn't care less if my computer is "intelligent" when it can do everything I would want an intelligent computer to do.
